annotations.title: Fetch missing receipts from supplier portals

description:
Start one Well cloud browser run, in the background, that signs in to each named supplier's portal with the person's saved login, finds the invoices of the named payments, downloads their PDFs and attaches each one to its payment. Use it only on WhatsApp, and only when the person explicitly asked to fetch the receipts as a background task (« en tâche de fond », « in the background »): without that ask, a supplier's portal goes through the Well extension. Use it for leads of well_list_missing_invoices whose `available_routes` holds `cloud_portal_fetch` and that the person picked, by number or by name, from the numbered recap you sent in an earlier turn. The background ask is not a pick: send the recap with its numbered leads first, and start nothing in that turn. Call it once per workspace with every picked portal lead of that workspace: at most 5 suppliers.

For each supplier pass the row's `company_id` and the `id` of each of its `transactions`, never a transaction of another row. Well reads the portal address of the supplier itself. Never pass a supplier the person did not pick.

The run never pays and never clicks a button of the site. Well sends the outcome to the person on WhatsApp itself. For a supplier the person has no saved login for, Well sends a link to a Well page where the person saves the login, waits, and picks that supplier up again on its own once the login is saved. Never ask the person to send a login or a password in the conversation. Follow the result's `message`: never say a receipt was found or attached. On a later question about these receipts, read well_list_missing_invoices again: the report reaches the person outside this conversation.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

run_in_background.description: Always true: the person's own message explicitly asked to fetch these receipts as a background task. Without that ask, do not call this tool.

suppliers.description: The picked portal leads of this workspace, at most 5.

transaction_ids.description: The `id` of each of the row's `transactions`, at most 10.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_create_portal_fetch

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

skipped_transaction_ids.description: Payments left out: they already have a document, or carry no amount or date.

title: Fetch missing receipts from supplier portals
